newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK NBS HEAD TO DISCUSS LATEST MONETARY MOVES.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK NBS HEAD TO DISCUSS LATEST MONETARY MOVES.

text.p: National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) Governor Vladimir Masar will meet journalists on Thursday at 1400 local time (1300 gmt) to discuss recent monetary developments and the Slovak banking sector, the NBS said.

"We will inform about the latest monetary indicators and the situation in the banking sector. The meeting's agenda includes no such issues as the Lombard or discount rates or credit limits," NBS spokesman Jan Onda told Reuters.
The news conference will take place shortly after a regular Thursday meeting of the NBS board with heads of NBS divisions.

On Wednesday, the NBS raised its bill repurchase rate by 70 basis points to 9.7 percent, but left the reverse repo rate unchanged at 7.2 percent. The central bank has yet to comment publicly on the move.

The hike pushed Slovak interbank money market offered rates up to the range of 13.2-14.93 percent an all maturities on Thursday, and prompted dealers to question whether a hike in the Lombard rate, the NBS last-resort lending facility, might be coming soon.

The Lombard rate was raised to 15 percent from 13 percent on July 17, as the central bank began tightening monetary policy. However dealers noted that the repo rate is more relevant to the market than the Lombard.
The NBS's primary lending rate, the discount rate, was last changed in January to 8.80 percent from 9.75 percent.
